rubrics.rubric: Does price_benchmark_analysis.csv correctly derive per-commodity benchmarks from the instructed government dataset?
criterion: The CSV has exactly the six required columns.
Records are limited to reasonably matching electrical, plumbing, and safety commodity titles from the instructed dataset and codes.
Unit cost is Encumbered Amount divided by Encumbered Quantity only when quantity is greater than zero.
Record count, average, median, and maximum are computed separately for each commodity title within each category.
The reported statistics are reproducible from the retrieved source records.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Line Item Comparison accurately consolidate the bids and apply defensible benchmark flags?
criterion: All 15 requisition line items appear once with the requested quantities.
Quoted unit and extended prices for all three suppliers agree with supplier_bid_proposals.xlsx.
Supplier totals reconcile to the line-item extensions.
Each reasonable historical match uses the matched commodity's median unit cost.
Each supplier-item quote receives its own Above Benchmark, Below Benchmark, Within Range, or No Benchmark classification using the instructed 20 percent thresholds.
No Benchmark is used when no reasonably comparable commodity exists.
Any proxy commodity match is identified clearly enough to evaluate its comparability.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Weighted Evaluation score all suppliers consistently on the five instructed criteria?
criterion: Price Competitiveness is weighted 30 percent.
Delivery Lead Time is weighted 25 percent.
Payment Terms, Warranty Coverage, and Additional Value are each weighted 15 percent.
Every supplier receives a 1-to-5 score and a source-grounded justification for every criterion.
Weighted totals are calculated correctly from the displayed scores and weights.
The ranking is consistent with the displayed weighted totals.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Split-Award Analysis compare single-source and category-level split scenarios on a complete total-cost basis?
criterion: The bid evaluation workbook contains exactly the three sheets Line Item Comparison, Weighted Evaluation, and Split-Award Analysis.
Scenario A uses the top-ranked supplier's quoted prices for all 15 items.
Scenario B assigns each category to a documented best-value supplier and shows separate category or PO subtotals.
Freight is applied to each modeled supplier order using that supplier's threshold and FOB terms.
Early-payment savings use the quoted discount terms.
Early-payment annualized returns use discount percent multiplied by 365 divided by net days minus discount days.
Volume discounts are treated separately and applied only to qualifying supplier order amounts.
Warranty differences are included as a quantified value or a documented qualitative TCO factor.
The displayed scenario totals reconcile to their merchandise, freight, discount, and warranty components.

rubrics.rubric: Does the analysis evaluate safety-item delivery against the OSHA remediation window and provide a workable mitigation plan?
criterion: The PR-2025-0043 submission date, required date, and three-week OSHA window are identified.
Each supplier's safety lead-time range is converted from business days to calendar weeks using the instructed conversion.
Each supplier receives a source-grounded compliance-risk classification.
Safety items are assigned only to a supplier reasonably capable of meeting the three-week window.
The memo provides actionable mitigation proportionate to any remaining delivery uncertainty.

rubrics.rubric: Do the purchase orders form a complete and accurate authorization set for the recommended strategy?
criterion: One clearly authoritative PO set corresponds to the recommended award strategy.
A single-source award uses PO-2025-0112, while a split award uses separate supplier files numbered PO-2025-0112A, PO-2025-0112B, and so on.

Each PO follows the provided template's observable structure by including a purchase-order header, PO number and date, supplier or bill-to and ship-to blocks, shipping, payment, and delivery fields, and a line-item table; cosmetic style matching is not required.
Each PO references the applicable requisition numbers.
Each PO uses the selected supplier's quoted line-item prices.
Each PO states the supplier's payment, delivery, FOB, discount, and freight terms.
Each PO shows category subtotals, freight, and grand total.
Each PO uses the required ClearFlow Water Services ship-to address.

rubrics.rubric: Does the procurement package demonstrate compliance with the $35,000 quarterly threshold?
criterion: The sum of the recommended PO grand totals including freight is shown on a pre-discount basis.
The recommended pre-discount commitment does not exceed $35,000.
Each supplier's full-order merchandise plus applicable freight is separately checked against $35,000.
Contingent discounts are not used to create apparent threshold compliance.

rubrics.rubric: Does the procurement decision memo contain the required addressee, ordered sections, and supporting analysis?
criterion: The memo is a valid DOCX addressed to Sarah Chen, Operations Director.
The five required memo sections appear in the instructed order.
The benchmark section identifies material pricing anomalies and limits of the historical comparisons.
The scenario section gives dollar figures for single-source and split-award options.
The recommendation section explains the selected strategy.
The OSHA section states the delivery risk and mitigation.
The budget-code section maps each requisition or category to its supplied budget code.

rubrics.rubric: Is the recommended award strategy a source-grounded best-value decision consistent across the workbook, memo, and POs?
criterion: The recommendation considers price, delivery, payment terms, warranty, and additional value.
The treatment of pump warranty coverage reflects the actual supplier terms and the value at risk.
The selected suppliers and dollar totals are consistent across the analysis, memo, and authoritative POs.
The recommendation explains why the chosen strategy is preferable to the modeled alternative without assuming a predetermined supplier.
